title: Soliton Profiles in 1D: Enhanced Neural-Network Solvers and Constrained Deep Ritz Methods
authors: Chandler Haight, Alex D Rodriguez, Svetlana Roudenko
abstract: We develop and compare enhanced neural-network solvers for one-dimensional ground-state profiles, which are solutions of $$ Q^{\prime\prime}=bQ-γQ^{p},\quad Q>0,\quad p>1, \quad b, γ>0, $$ the stationary profile equation for the nonlinear Schrödinger, generalized Korteweg-de Vries, and nonlinear Klein-Gordon equations. Its explicit sech-type solutions serve as exact reference for error computation and benchmark hyperparameter selection. We improve on the standard Adam-trained physics-informed neural network (PINN) baseline by introducing higher-order optimization via Gauss-Newton/Levenberg-Marquardt and L-BFGS refinements, as well as Fourier-feature PINNs, and constrained Deep Ritz (DR) formulations. In DR approaches we introduce two new neural-network formulations, which implement two classical variational characterizations: a Nehari-constrained Deep Ritz method, in which the height is learned by projecting onto the Nehari/Pokhozhaev manifold, and a Weinstein Deep Ritz method, in which a normalized profile minimizes the Weinstein quotient. The Deep Ritz formulations perform best overall, in particular, the Weinstein variant gives the best error-runtime balance. The neural-network based solvers remain less accurate and efficient than classical Petviashvili iteration in 1D, however, the current study provides a proof of concept: the mesh-free formulation, non-reliance on exact profiles or the related features make them promising in higher dimensions and for more complicated nonlinearities and dispersive operators.
summary: This work compares advanced neural network techniques, including constrained Deep Ritz methods, for numerically solving the ground-state profiles of nonlinear dispersive equations. The methods are benchmarked against classical solvers, showing that variational deep learning approaches are highly promising for extending to higher dimensions and complex physical models beyond the 1D proof-of-concept.
main_problem: The paper develops and compares enhanced neural-network solvers for finding one-dimensional ground-state profiles, which are solutions to a stationary profile equation derived from nonlinear dispersive PDEs.
main_result: The constrained Deep Ritz formulations, particularly the Weinstein variant, perform best, achieving the best error-runtime balance, although they remain less accurate than classical methods in 1D.
method: The authors compare standard PINNs against enhanced versions incorporating higher-order optimization (Gauss-Newton/L-BFGS) and advanced variational techniques like Nehari and Weinstein constrained Deep Ritz methods.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the ground-state profile equation, $Q'' = bQ - \gamma|Q|^{p-1}Q$, which governs solitary wave solutions for nonlinear Schrödinger, generalized Korteweg-de Vries, and nonlinear Klein-Gordon equations.
key_observables: Ground-state profiles (solitary waves), $L^2$ errors, and computational runtime.
important_parameters: Nonlinearity exponent $p$ ($p>1$), and physical constants $b$ and $\gamma$.
main_assumptions: The 1D case is used as a controlled benchmark due to the existence of explicit sech-type solutions; the methods are presented as a proof of concept for higher dimensions.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the physical problem (soliton profiles) and the governing ODE. It then details the comparison between various neural network solvers (PINNs, FF-PINNs, Deep Ritz) and benchmarks them against classical methods, culminating in a discussion of the performance trade-offs.
why_interesting: While focused on classical nonlinear PDEs, the development of robust, variational deep learning solvers (Deep Ritz) provides powerful, generalizable numerical tools applicable to complex, high-dimensional quantum field theories or many-body Hamiltonians where traditional solvers struggle.
